subject.question: Can any of the four original sequential catalog observations be reused or coalesced while preserving the current readiness, source, owner, fence, case and deadline requirements?

decision.summary: The repeated catalog function is used at distinct admission/readiness boundaries. The current first Host post-open readiness call must remain fresh: complete existing actual-provider tests explicitly change or fail the catalog after factory.open and require the first checkReadiness to await and reject that new observation. A same-binding cached success would violate those cases. D's two checks are separately required by its current test and protect pre-thread configuration and post-thread tools.
decision.doesNotEstablish: This does not prove that every implementation must always perform four subprocess catalog reads. It proves that merely caching one success under the currently available identities and contracts does not preserve the selected behavior, and that the retained failure does not establish which underlying operation consumed its time.
decision.casesAndDeadlines: No existing case, assertion, original 15-second outer readiness wait, 25 ms poll cadence, inner provider bound, cleanup requirement or authority check is removed or changed.

observationBoundaries.anchor: RuntimeOwner.allocate after factory return, attachment, allocated/owned publication, observer start and sealed-state check
observationBoundaries.freshFact: A new D readiness result is obtained after the returned session is attached to the Host. The Host provider sets its own ready flag only after that result and its currentness check; RuntimeOwner publishes nativeReady only if readiness and required capabilities pass and the record remains allocated/unsealed.
observationBoundaries.otherGuards: The same source's currentness, captured process running state, app MCP selection, record phase/seal, capability requirements, and future per-input D readiness remain separate.
observationBoundaries.concreteCounterexample: The current actual-provider same/different/throws cases change the catalog immediately after factory.open, then perform the first wrapped checkReadiness. Only same may be ready. The exact four-call diagnostic-preservation case also remains part of the existing whole file.
observationBoundaries.whyPriorStateIsInsufficient: A successful D factory return contains no consumable readiness receipt, no native mutation epoch, and no lock protecting the subsequent Host publication interval.

sourceOpenFlow: RuntimeOwner.open runs prepareSessionOpen in a synchronous Runtime fence and persists opening intent before allocation.
The fenced call returns before allocate awaits options.driverFactory.open.

After factory.open resolves, allocate attaches the exact returned session, validates sessionRef, and separately publishes sessionRef/custody/allocated or closing state. Current admission or authority loss marks the record sealed.
It starts the existing observer. A sealed record goes to original owned cleanup.
It then awaits opened.driver.checkReadiness and separately publishes nativeReady under the current allocated/unsealed record guard plus required-capability inclusion.
No one synchronous fence spans native initialization, thread creation, D post-open readiness and the later Host readiness publication.
transactionAnalysis.factoryContract: The full current D factory returns exactly { driver, capabilities }; success implies its earlier mandatory check passed, but no proof object, validity interval, native metadata version or single-consumption token is returned.
transactionAnalysis.capturedSourceMeaning: capturedMcpSourceCurrent reads and normalizes the selected captured app/Claude MCP catalog source and deep-compares capturedMcpServers. It does not attest all original native Codex configured/plugin metadata, native config/read or thread server status.
transactionAnalysis.sealedMeaning: A sealed provider/record prevents further admission. A sealed source identity or identical request/digest is not an immutable lease on all native configuration and live thread state.
transactionAnalysis.noAtomicityClaim: The current checks themselves are finite observations rather than a continuously atomic native snapshot. This advisory neither invents atomicity for them nor uses their existing finite nature to justify deleting a later observation.

findings.finding: All 17 complete source/test bodies have exact immutable blob/byte/SHA joins; their total is 235,253 bytes.
The selected Host/D path has three catalog checks before factory.open returns and one new catalog check during the first Host readiness call.
Pre-allocation, pre-thread, post-thread and post-attachment checks guard distinct boundaries, even though they share verifyCatalog.
The Runtime fence does not hold native metadata immutable across those awaits. State publications and native observations are separate.
Current D return data has no explicit reusable native readiness proof or mutation epoch.
Captured app MCP source equality is narrower than original native Codex catalog/config/status equality.
Existing first post-open same/different/throws cases provide a concrete counterexample to ordinary success caching while identities remain the same.
The current exact four-call assertion and D's exact two-call assertion would be changed by simple coalescing.
D's native config/read and thread MCP status calls are fresh protocol requests; a catalog digest alone does not substitute for them.
Every later input still requires D readiness before turn/start; Host-ready and native-ready flags do not grant unrestricted input authority.

The failed Windows receipt identifies catalog invocation 6 as outstanding only in its saved non-atomic projection. It does not prove whether launch, stdout, exit or disposal was the expensive component.
Four calls alone do not prove the 15-second deadline failure was caused by redundant work; no repaired runtime outcome is asserted.

No source-proved minimal coalescing fix preserves all current cases/guards under the available contract. The no-change conclusion is scoped to simple reuse within current contracts, not an impossibility theorem for a redesigned provider protocol.
No source/control candidate, new test implementation, runtime attempt, venue, approval gate or replay was authored or selected.

boundedNextDecision.safeImmediateAdvice: Preserve the four original checks and their failure behavior. Do not infer native catalog immutability from source/binding equality, bypass the first Host readiness observation, or treat D factory success as Host input authority.
boundedNextDecision.exactMissingReuseInvariant: A legitimate reuse design would have to establish that the very native catalog/config/thread facts used by D remain valid through the Host publication boundary, including changes/errors/abort/owner revocation that the current first-post-open tests detect. Current source supplies neither such a native validity witness nor an atomic interval. This statement identifies the missing semantic proof; it does not select a new API, test or gate.
boundedNextDecision.exactMissingPerformanceFact: The retained failure has no direct per-invocation correlation from catalog invocation 6 to a particular native preparation plus its launch/first-stdout/terminal/disposal subintervals. Therefore it cannot distinguish startup/hash/controller latency from native metadata work or cleanup. Any later evidence capture remains root-selected and must preserve original behavior and budgets.
boundedNextDecision.meaningfulExistingDiscriminators: The complete current Host same/different/throws cases, exact-four work equality, pre-allocation refusal, D pre/post-thread ordering and per-input drift checks already discriminate a naive cache. They must remain intact; this advisory does not append or replace them.

limits: Source-only feasibility; no test or target source was executed.

No claim that original A/B configured version constants prove both publication probes ran.
No new runtime, GUI, native or whole-suite qualification.
Original test case inventories, process authority, deadlines, cleanup and unknown-state behavior remain unchanged.
